instruction: Let \( V \) denote the space of all polynomials with real coefficients having degree at most \( n \). Define \( D: V \to V \) by \( D(p(x)) = \frac{dp}{dx} \). Find the annihilator of the image of \( D \).

2. The differentiation operator \( D \) maps a polynomial \( p(x) \) to its derivative \( p'(x) \). The image of \( D \), denoted \( \text{Im}(D) \), is the set of all polynomials of degree at most \( n-1 \), which is the subspace \( V_{n-1} \).
3. The annihilator of \( \text{Im}(D) \), denoted \( (\text{Im}(D))^\circ \), is the set of all linear functionals \( f \) in the dual space \( V^* \) such that \( f(w) = 0 \) for all \( w \in \text{Im}(D) \).
4. Since \( \text{Im}(D) = V_{n-1} \), the annihilator consists of all linear functionals that vanish on all polynomials of degree at most \( n-1 \).
5. The annihilator is a one-dimensional subspace of \( V^* \). It is spanned by the functional that evaluates the \( n \)-th derivative at 0, which corresponds to extracting the coefficient of \( x^n \) in a polynomial.

Thus, the annihilator of the image of \( D \) is the set of all linear functionals that annihilate polynomials of degree at most \( n-1 \). This is spanned by the functional that evaluates the \( n \)-th derivative at 0.
